---
title: "Episode 8: The Data Room"
subtitle: "Programming with Python · Tutorial 08"
---

The investor wasn't impressed by a slide. She was impressed by *data*. So she
slides a USB stick across the table: **every order, two full weeks.** "Impress
me." That stick is now a real file, `orders_messy.csv`. Tobi exported it from
the ordering system and nobody has looked at it since. It has too many rows to
eyeball and too many for a hand-written loop, so this week you use the tool
built for exactly this: **pandas**. You'll load the file into one *DataFrame*,
filter it with boolean masks, add a derived column on a safe copy, and answer
per-zone questions with `groupby`. Tobi, meanwhile, has discovered AI. Your
real job is to **supervise** it and catch the confident nonsense.

## Run the lab on your laptop

From this episode the lab is a Python script that runs on your own machine, in
the `python-labs` folder you created in Session VII.

1. Download both files and move them into your `python-labs` folder:

   [Lab script](../labs/lab_08_dataroom.py){.btn .btn-primary download="lab_08_dataroom.py"}
   [Orders data](../labs/orders_messy.csv){.btn .btn-primary download="orders_messy.csv"}

2. In Zed, open the `python-labs` folder, then the terminal (`` Ctrl+` ``).
3. Run `uv run python lab_08_dataroom.py`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## No Zed on your laptop, or only an iPad?

Use a **GitHub codespace**: a Linux computer that runs in a browser tab.

1. Sign in at [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces) and start
   the **Blank** template. If you set one up in Session VII, open it again and
   go to step 3.
2. In its terminal, follow the [uv guide](../general/uv.qmd) (the macOS or
   Linux lines) down to `uv add pandas matplotlib`.
3. Go into the folder with `cd python-labs` and download both files:

   ```bash
   curl -O https://python.tobiasvlcek.com/labs/lab_08_dataroom.py
   curl -O https://python.tobiasvlcek.com/labs/orders_messy.csv
   ```

4. Run `uv run python lab_08_dataroom.py`.

A codespace has no Zed, so keep the chatbot open in a second tab for AI help.
:::

The first run prints three tables and then stops with
`AssertionError: Task 1: not attempted yet.` That is the lab working: the
script checks every task and stops at the first one you have not solved yet.
Solve it, save, and run again.

::: {.callout-important}
## Look at your numbers

Each task gives you a symptom ("Hafen is missing orders"), and you find the
cause. The checks only test the form of your answers, so a wrong number can
pass all of them. And **one problem in the export is not mentioned anywhere**:
no task names it and no check catches it.
:::

When every check passes, the script prints a block that starts with
`SHOW THIS IN CLASS`. Show it to your lecturer, and you are free to go.
